# HarvestMath

> Free, mobile-friendly gardening calculators covering soil, mulch, fertilizer, watering, spacing, lawns, trees, indoor plants, hydroponics, and greenhouses — no sign-up required.

HarvestMath.com provides calculators for home gardeners, landscapers, and houseplant owners, organized into 8 clusters. Each calculator page includes a worked example, common mistakes, and an FAQ section. All calculators run entirely in the browser — no data is sent to a server.

## Calculators

- [Cubic Yard Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/cubic-yard-calculator/): converts between cubic yards, cubic feet, tons, and dimensions for soil, gravel, or mulch — a unit-conversion tool, not a how-much-do-I-need calculator
- [Topsoil Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/topsoil-calculator/): calculates topsoil volume in cubic feet, cubic yards, tons, and bags
- [Raised Bed Soil Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/raised-bed-soil-calculator/): soil volume and mix ratio for raised beds, with common size presets
- [Soil Volume Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/soil-volume-calculator/): soil volume for rectangular beds and cylindrical pots/containers
- [Mulch Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/mulch-calculator/): mulch volume for rectangular and circular beds, plus a bale count for pine straw
- [Plant Spacing Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/plant-spacing-calculator/): plant count and layout by crop, row or square-foot method, plus a Trees & Shrubs mode with real mature spacing for fruit trees, pecans, and landscape shrubs
- [Grass Seed Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/grass-seed-calculator/): seed quantity by grass type, new lawn or overseeding
- [Overseeding Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/overseeding-calculator/): seed and topdressing amounts to overseed an existing lawn, by grass type and condition
- [Sod Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/sod-calculator/): square footage, pallets, and pieces of sod needed, by grass type, lawn shape, and waste factor
- [Tree Age Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/tree-age-calculator/): estimates tree age from trunk circumference without cutting it down
- [NPK Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/npk-calculator/): fertilizer application rate, liquid dilution, and multi-fertilizer blending
- [Pot Size Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/pot-size-calculator/): pot size conversion, repotting sizing, and container guide by plant
- [Frost Date Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/frost-date-calculator/): estimated frost dates and planting timeline by hardiness zone
- [Compost Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/compost-calculator/): compost volume, bags, and weight for beds and top-dressing
- [Soil Type Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/soil-type-calculator/): classifies soil texture using the USDA soil triangle, from sand/silt/clay percentages or jar test measurements
- [Seed Starting Calendar](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/seed-starting-calculator/): personalized seed-starting and transplant schedule by frost date
- [Drip Irrigation Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/drip-irrigation-calculator/): run time and water delivered based on emitter flow rate
- [Rain Barrel Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/rain-barrel-calculator/): rainwater collection from roof area and rainfall, plus spigot water pressure
- [USDA Hardiness Zone Finder](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/hardiness-zone-finder/): find your exact USDA plant hardiness zone by ZIP code, plus the average annual minimum winter temperature range it represents
- [Grow Light & DLI Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/grow-light-calculator/): grow light coverage, wattage, DLI, and hanging distance
- [Vegetable Yield Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/vegetable-yield-calculator/): estimated harvest yield by crop and area
- [Growing Degree Days Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/growing-degree-days-calculator/): converts daily high/low temps into GDD/GDU with base temperature presets, the 86/50 cap, and single-day or season-long accumulation tracking
- [Tree Height Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/tree-height-calculator/): measures a tree's height three ways -- clinometer angle (with slope correction for sloped ground), shadow ratio, or the stick method
- [Greenhouse Heater Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/greenhouse-heater-calculator/): estimated heat loss and recommended heater size (BTU) by shape, glazing, and climate
- [Hydroponic Nutrient Calculator](https://harvestmath.com/calculators/hydroponic-nutrient-calculator/): scale any nutrient product's label dose by reservoir size and growth stage, plus EC-to-PPM conversion on the 500/640/700 scales

## Guides

- [Why Are My Plant Leaves Turning Yellow? A Diagnostic Guide](https://harvestmath.com/blog/why-are-my-plant-leaves-turning-yellow/): the first entry in the Plant Problem Diagnosis category -- diagnoses yellowing leaves across any plant using the mobile-vs-immobile nutrient framework (old growth vs. new growth), covers nitrogen/magnesium/potassium/iron/manganese deficiencies, overwatering, underwatering, natural aging, and transplant shock, with a scannable symptom-to-fix table
- [How to Start a Vegetable Garden: A Complete Beginner's Guide](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-start-a-vegetable-garden/): the beginner hub page -- an 8-step decision sequence from finding a sunny spot through soil prep (including the lead-safety soil test point most guides skip) to watering and mulch, routing into all six crop guides, the raised bed guide, and ten calculators
- [Why Are My Tomato Leaves Turning Yellow? A Diagnostic Guide](https://harvestmath.com/blog/why-are-my-tomato-leaves-turning-yellow/): the third piece in the tomato series -- a scannable symptom-first diagnostic table, bottom-up yellowing vs. nitrogen deficiency, early blight vs. septoria leaf spot told apart by the spot itself, and honest, non-curable-disease treatment guidance
- [Growing Tomatoes in Raised Beds: Spacing, Depth, and Blossom End Rot](https://harvestmath.com/blog/growing-tomatoes-in-raised-beds/): the companion piece to the tomato seed-starting guide -- bed depth, tighter raised-bed spacing math with a plants-per-bed-size table, the standard soil mix, and why raised beds are specifically more prone to blossom end rot (with the calcium myth corrected)
- [How to Grow Beans from Seed (Bush, Pole, and the Nitrogen Myth)](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-beans-from-seed/): the sixth pattern in the seed-starting cluster -- direct-sow only, bush vs. pole tradeoffs, and an honest correction of the popular "beans fix your soil" myth using real nitrogen-fixation figures, nodule diagnostics, and inoculant guidance
- [How to Grow Cucumbers from Seed (and Why Yours Aren't Fruiting)](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-cucumbers-from-seed/): the fifth pattern in the seed-starting cluster -- cucumbers work either direct-sown or transplanted, the paper towel germination method, why plants flower heavily but fail to fruit (separate male and female flowers), hand pollination, and cucumber beetles as the bacterial wilt vector
- [How to Grow Carrots from Seed (and Actually Get Them to Germinate)](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-carrots-from-seed/): the direct-sow-only pattern in the seed-starting cluster -- the board method for fixing germination, deep loose soil for straight roots, thinning, containers, and troubleshooting forked/stunted/bolted/hairy roots
- [How to Grow Lettuce from Seed: The Cool-Season Crop That Breaks the Rules](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-lettuce-from-seed/): the direct-sow, cool-season counterpoint to the tomato and pepper guides -- lettuce needs light (not darkness) to germinate, cool soil (not warmth), succession sowing, bolting, containers, and honest coverage of regrowing store-bought lettuce from a stub
- [How to Grow Peppers from Seed: Bell, Hot, and Sweet Varieties](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-peppers-from-seed/): full seed-starting process for peppers -- timing anchored to our Seed Starting Calculator, why peppers need more warmth and time than tomatoes, the transplant depth difference from tomatoes, and variety-specific notes for bell, jalapeno, habanero, serrano, and super-hots
- [How to Grow Tomatoes from Seed: A Complete Guide](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-grow-tomatoes-from-seed/): full seed-starting process for tomatoes -- timing anchored to our Seed Starting Calculator, the heat-mat-to-light transition mistake, damping off prevention, and variety-specific notes for cherry, roma, beefsteak, and heirloom
- [LED vs. Fluorescent Grow Lights: Which Should You Use?](https://harvestmath.com/blog/led-vs-fluorescent-grow-lights/): LED vs. fluorescent grow lights compared on efficiency, running cost, lifespan, mercury/disposal, and the specific case where fluorescent still makes sense (seed starting)
- [What Can (and Can't) You Compost? The Complete List](https://harvestmath.com/blog/what-can-you-compost/): what you can and can't put in your compost bin, a Bokashi anaerobic-fermentation exception, and by-bin-type notes for tumblers, open piles, and worm bins
- [15 Homemade Fertilizers You Can Make at Home (and How to Mix Them)](https://harvestmath.com/blog/15-homemade-fertilizers-you-can-make-at-home/): 15 real homemade fertilizers with genuine depth per item, an N-P-K reference table, and honest cautions on wood ash and fresh manure
- [Companion Planting Chart: What to Grow Together (and What to Avoid)](https://harvestmath.com/blog/companion-planting-chart/): an interactive companion planting chart covering 6 vegetables and 4 herbs, plus common pairings, pest-control uses, and pairings to avoid
- [Organic vs. Inorganic Mulch: Which Is Right for Your Garden?](https://harvestmath.com/blog/organic-vs-inorganic-mulch/): the real difference between organic and inorganic mulch, and which one fits vegetable gardens, planting beds, pathways, and xeriscaping
- [How to Read and Understand Your Soil Test Results](https://harvestmath.com/blog/how-to-read-soil-test-results/): what pH, organic matter, N-P-K, and micronutrient readings on a soil test actually mean, and how to turn them into a fertilizer plan
- [Succession Planting: How to Get More Harvests From the Same Space](https://harvestmath.com/blog/succession-planting/): the three real succession planting methods (staggered sowing, staggered-maturity varieties, interplanting) with a worked raised-bed example
- [8 Fertilizing Mistakes That Are Hurting Your Garden and Lawn](https://harvestmath.com/blog/8-fertilizing-mistakes-hurting-your-garden-and-lawn/): the most common fertilizing mistakes, from over-application to bad timing, and how to avoid and fix each one
- [How to Build a Rainwater Collection System for Your Garden](https://harvestmath.com/blog/rainwater-collection-system/): step-by-step rain barrel setup covering downspout connection, first-flush filtering, overflow routing, and winterizing
- [8 Mulch Mistakes That Are Secretly Hurting Your Plants](https://harvestmath.com/blog/8-mulch-mistakes-hurting-your-plants/): the most common mulching mistakes, from volcano mulching to guessing the amount, and how to avoid each one
- [Cool-Season vs. Warm-Season Grass: Which Type Do You Have?](https://harvestmath.com/blog/cool-season-vs-warm-season-grass/): the C3/C4 photosynthesis difference behind cool-season and warm-season grass, how to tell which you have, and what to plant in the transition zone
- [Topsoil vs. Garden Soil: What’s the Difference?](https://harvestmath.com/blog/topsoil-vs-garden-soil/): explains how topsoil and garden soil differ and which one to use for a given project
